newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate drops to 10.7 pct from 12.6.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate drops to 10.7 pct from 12.6.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate dropped to 10.7 percent on Tuesday from 12.6 percent as supply overshot demand for kuna funds in thin trade.
Total settlements halved to 22.3 million kuna. Borrowers asked for another 2.7 million kuna but could not agree on terms with lenders.
Renewed term deals totalled 5.8 million kuna, while most of fresh borrowings were granted at a steady call money rate of 10.5 percent.
Insurers charged nine percent for one week loans and banks rolled over previous two-week grants at 14 and 16 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 5.9424 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5662 against the mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
